title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval & Regression Checks
next_steps: Redwood to share updated evaluation spreadsheet with per-prompt scores
Customer to run regression tests on last 48 hours of logs and share sample failures
Schedule deep-dive performance call w/ Tom next week to discuss VPC networking constraints
action_items: Sofia: Share evaluation spreadsheet and prompt set links by 2026-03-12
Rita: Run regression on 3 recent failing prompts and post examples by 2026-03-13
Marcus: Put together a short doc on guardrail tuning and template changes by 2026-03-15
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality eval results, discuss a small regression on a subset of prompts after model tweak, and align on prompt-set scoring and guardrail changes. Agreement to share artifacts and run deeper regression checks. Plan a network/VPC deep dive for perf tuning.
topics: next steps and artifacts to share
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're at our weekly cadence for the POC, quick roll call?
[00:06] David (Aurora): David here.
[00:08] Rita (Aurora): Rita.
[00:09] Tom (Aurora): Tom.
[00:10] Leah (Aurora): Leah here.
[00:12] Marcus (Redwood): Marcus, hi.
[00:13] Priya (Redwood): Priya joining.
[00:15] Sofia: Cool. Agenda — quick review of last week's quality eval, dig into the small regression Rita flagged, then next steps. Marcus, do you want to start with the eval highlights?
[00:25] Marcus: Yeah, sure. So we ran the 120-case prompt set through the tuned model variant (we called it redwood-v1-tuned). Overall macro accuracy held steady: 87% pass rate by our rubric, which is +1% versus baseline, and latency is about the same on hosted. The issues we saw are concentrated in the 'financial-summarization' prompts — some hallucination and bad entity linking.
[00:43] Rita: Right, we saw a few runs where the model added incorrect ticker mappings, like it turned "ACME" into a different company, it's subtle but it fails our downstream mapping.
[00:52] David: Is that from the new priming we added last week or from quantization changes? I thought you mentioned you shipped a small quant profile.
[00:58] Marcus: Good call — we did a light quantization step for the dedicated variant to reduce memory, but the tuned weights are the same. The quant profile might change token probabilities slightly. We compared non-quant vs quant and the diff is small but visible on those edge cases.
[01:14] Sofia: Ok so possible root causes: prompt template change, quantization, or data drift in your test set. Rita, do you have examples?
[01:21] Rita: Yeah I pulled 5 failing prompts — I'll paste them in the doc after the call but short version: when asked to map entity mentions to internal ids, there are 2-3 where it chooses an older product name. The prompt uses a couple of aliases — the model seems to prefer older alias.
[01:34] Marcus: That points to prompt weighting. We saw similar in another POC where stronger alias disambiguation in the prompt and adding a small retrieval hint fixed it.
[01:42] Leah: We also noticed some inconsistency with the guardrail — sometimes the output triggers the rejection rule, sometimes not. It's like thresholding instability.
[01:51] Marcus: That's likely scoring threshold sensitivity — our scoring uses normalized BLEU-ish + entity match. When logits shift slightly due to quant, the score can drift across the cutoff.
[02:02] Tom: From the SRE perspective, latency was stable on hosted, but when we tried the dedicated private sim our p99 jumped ~40ms because of VPC egress rules — we're still seeing that.
[02:12] Sofia: Noted. We'll put a VPC deep-dive on the calendar. For quality, immediate steps are: share per-prompt scoring and examples, run non-quant baseline on the same inputs, and adjust guardrail thresholds if warranted.
[02:27] Marcus: I uploaded preliminary eval CSV to the shared drive (link in notes). Key columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, model_variant, score, pass_fail, notes. The cluster of failures is prompt_ids 34, 47, 89 — mostly entity alias edge cases.
[02:42] Rita: That matches what we saw. One oddity — prompt 47 sometimes passes when we add a short explicit instruction "prefer latest product name". So it's a prompting fix as well.
[02:53] Sofia: Great — two prongs: prompt-set fix + scoreboard tuning. Marcus, can you walk through scoring thresholds?
[02:59] Marcus: Sure. For this POC we set a pass cutoff of 0.72 overall. The scoring is an ensemble: exact entity match (weight 0.6), semantic similarity (0.25), and length/format checks (0.15). If entity match drops from 0.9 to 0.7 due to token reorder it can flip pass->fail. We can make the threshold slightly more robust or add a per-prompt override table for known edge cases.
[03:26] David: Per-prompt overrides might be easiest short-term for the pilot. Long term we want the model to generalize.
[03:32] Priya: Also gating on confidence and surfacing low-confidence examples to your team for review would help. We can tag them in the dashboard.
[03:40] Rita: Can you also explain why some outputs bypass the guardrail? The guardrail is supposed to reject non-financial answers; sometimes it lets them through.
[03:47] Marcus: Our guardrail check is a regex+classifier combo. The classifier's threshold is tuned for recall; if token probs shift the classifier score dips below rejection, so we end up with false negatives. The fix is to either harden the regex for critical fields or run a second downstream classifier as a fallback.
[04:05] Leah: Hardening regex could be brittle but for a few critical fields it's acceptable.
[04:09] Tom: On the infra side, if we move to Private deployment with your VPC, we can pin model variant to non-quant for the pilot to remove one variable. That buys time while we test quantized performance.
[04:19] Sofia: Good suggestion. Marcus, can you produce a non-quant artifact we can run in Aurora's test environment?
[04:24] Marcus: Yes. I can export the non-quant model snapshot and instructions. It requires ~24GB of GPU memory so we'll need to confirm your infra for private testing.
[04:33] Tom: We have a couple of machines that can run that, we'll check. Also want to schedule the networking deep-dive — our VPC NAT config looks like it's adding egress latency.
[04:44] David: Back to scoring — any chance the scoring script had a bug during the last run? Small off-by-one on tokenization can shift entity match.
[04:52] Marcus: We double-checked tokenization; the harness uses the same tokenizer as serving. But I want to re-run a non-quant baseline to be 100% sure.
[04:59] Rita: If you re-run, can you include the raw logits or at least confidence numbers for the failing cases? That'll help us triage.
[05:06] Marcus: Yep, I'll include confidence fields in the CSV.
[05:09] Sofia: On guardrails, Marcus you mentioned a second classifier — time estimate?
[05:13] Marcus: A simple binary classifier as fallback is quick — I can prototype in 2-3 days and test on the prompt set. If we need higher recall/precision tuning that might take another week.
[05:22] Priya: We'll prioritize the prototype for this week so you can validate.
[05:25] Leah: Also want a clearer definition of 'pass' for our PM metrics — currently it's a mix of correctness and format. Can we send a crisp success criteria doc?
[05:34] Sofia: Yes, we'll update the rubric and push it. I'll include explicit rules for entity mapping and allowed alias matching.
[05:41] Rita: One more note — we saw an unexplained regression on a previously passing prompt after a small prompt wording change. So we need to lock prompt templates during the regression window or version them.
[05:52] Marcus: Absolutely. We support prompt versioning in the harness. I'll enable per-prompt version tags and the evaluation will respect that.
[05:59] David: Ok, what's our plan for the next 7 days?
[06:03] Sofia: Action items: Marcus shares updated eval CSV + raw confidences and non-quant run by 2026-03-12; Rita runs regression tests and posts failing examples by 2026-03-13; Marcus prototypes fallback classifier by 2026-03-15; schedule VPC deep-dive w/ Tom for next week.
[06:21] Tom: For the VPC deep-dive, please include your network diagram and expected egress patterns.
[06:26] Sofia: We'll share a network-behavior doc. Also, we'll put together a short note on guardrail tuning best practices and a sample prompt template that addresses alias disambiguation.
[06:35] Leah: Any blockers on security/compliance side? We still need SOC2 artifact set and SSO test account to validate SAML flows for Private.
[06:43] Priya: We can share the SOC2 report and a temporary SSO test tenant. Marcus will coordinate SAML metadata.
[06:50] Marcus: I'll send the SAML metadata and steps. Expect they may need some firewall rules for the ACS endpoints.
[06:57] Rita: One practical question: if we tweak the pass threshold, how will you reflect that in historical dashboards? We don't want the weekly pass rate to flip retroactively.
[07:06] Marcus: We'll treat threshold changes as a new evaluation run and keep the prior runs immutable. Dashboard will show both historical baseline and the new run with tagging.
[07:15] David: Nice. About guardrail false positives — can we get a list of examples where guardrail rejected a valid response? That will help tune recall.
[07:23] Marcus: Yes, I'll add a "guardrail_fp_examples" sheet to the eval artifacts.
[07:27] Sofia: Anything else?
[07:29] Rita: Quick ask — can Redwood share a short note on how quantization typically impacts entity matching? Our infra team is worried quant will break important mappings.
[07:37] Marcus: I'll include a one-page note describing expected token-prob shifts and mitigation (prompting, per-prompt overrides, non-quant fallbacks).
[07:44] Tom: For the non-quant run in our test infra, what's needed credential-wise? We have ephemeral keys for your Private infra or do you need SSH?
[07:52] Marcus: We'll give a containerized test harness that uses the same API surface. So you won't need SSH, just a service account with Docker pull and run access. We'll share the instructions.
[08:05] Sofia: Ok let's recap: outputs to get after this call: updated eval CSV with confidences and non-quant runs, guardrail fp examples, prompt failure examples, SAML metadata, and short docs on quant effects + guardrail tuning. We'll post links in the CRM record.
[08:23] David: Sounds good.
[08:24] Leah: Thanks everyone.
[08:25] Sofia: Thanks — we'll follow up (end).
